name: oidc_login_attempts
description: Single-use binding between a browser login-attempt cookie and the OIDC state, nonce and PKCE verifier of one authorization request.
lifecycle: Created when a login starts, consumed once by the callback and expired after 10 minutes; expired rows are retained until a cleanup rule is approved.

columns.Meaning: Backend-generated attempt UUID that binds the sealed secrets.
SHA-256 of the random login-attempt cookie value.
OIDC state value expected back at the callback.
PKCE code verifier and OIDC nonce sealed with AES-256-GCM and bound to the attempt ID.
Validated same-origin relative path to open after a successful login.
Authentication context class (acr) this login requested, such as the strong teluni-aal2 level for step-up.
columns.Null meaning: A standard login without a requested level.

columns.Meaning: Maximum authentication age requested from the provider; 0 forces a new authentication for recent-authentication checks.
Instant after which the callback can no longer consume the attempt.
Instant the callback consumed the attempt; a second use is rejected.
columns.Null meaning: The attempt has not been used.

constraints.Purpose: An attempt expires after creation and within 10 minutes.
Handle hash is exactly one SHA-256 digest.
Requested maximum authentication age cannot be negative.
Return path is relative to the panel origin.
State uses the base64url alphabet and cannot be blank.

constraints.Physical definition: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX oidc_login_attempts_handle_hash_key ON public.oidc_login_attempts USING btree (handle_hash)
constraints.Purpose: One attempt per browser handle; supports consumption by handle.
